reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is a two-stream classification system where spatial tracking data (image) and statistical data (vector) are independently processed through dedicated neural networks (ConvNeXt and MLP), then fused via concatenation followed by a fully connected layer producing softmax probabilities over pass outcomes. The image stream encodes player positions and motion dynamics into a 768-dimensional feature space using a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny model, while the stats stream maps 15-dimensional seasonal metrics into a 64-d space via an MLP. These embeddings are concatenated and passed through a final classifier head. This structure enables explainability through stage-wise gradient attribution: first, modality-level contribution (C_B for image, C_S for stats) via summed signed gradients; second, within-modality importance (Grad-CAM for image, per-feature gradients for stats). The model assumes that a single frame captures sufficient context for prediction, which may fail under complex temporal dynamics or occlusions. It also assumes linear separability of modalities, potentially missing higher-order interactions. The dual nature of the model reflects a duality between geometric reasoning (spatial image) and relational reasoning (statistical network hubness), each contributing distinct but complementary signals to the final decision.
